predecessors.name: Western Roman Empire
predecessors.text: Britain, where 'early in 407, possibly February, his fellows acclaimed him as emperor', then Gaul

successors.name: Western Roman Empire
successors.text: Arles, where Constantine was besieged until Constantius 'arrived at Arles while Gerontius was outside the city'

ledger.x: early 407: the army in Britain acclaims Constantine emperor.
early 408: Constans takes Hispania for his father.
May 408: Constantine III holds Gaul from Arles.
early 411: Gerontius defeats Constans and besieges Constantine in Arles.

wars.name: Revolt of Constantine III
wars.outcome: Constantine held Britain from 407, Gaul and (through Constans) Hispania from 408, was recognised as co-emperor in early 409, lost Britain, Armorica and Hispania in 409, led an army into northern Italy in spring 410 and withdrew, lost the rest of Gaul to…

wars.name: Siege of Arles
wars.outcome: Gerontius and then Constantius besieged Constantine in Arles; he surrendered and was beheaded in August or September 411.

certainty.note: Provinces are named, not boundaries; the extent in Britain, Gaul and Hispania 407-410 is the Western Roman Empire's 406 shape in each region, and only Arles is certain in 411.

sources.title: End of Roman rule in Britain
